issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for Lecture.addGuestStudents: The problem statement (task description and UML) specifies a method addGuestStudents(int, String) — an int number of new guest students plus a String reason — but the solution implementation provides addGuestStudents(int) with a single int parameter. This discrepancy means students reading the exercise will be instructed to implement a two-parameter method while the provided solution uses a different signature, causing confusion and potential test/compilation mismatches when comparing implementations or using the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: update the solution implementation to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, String reason) (use or document the reason parameter, or store/log it) so it matches the problem statement and UML. Alternatively, if the reason parameter is intentionally unnecessary, update the problem statement, UML, and template instructions to specify addGuestStudents(int) and remove references to a reason. Ensure tests and examples are updated to match the chosen signature.
